This run crosses 542 context-vector recipes with 1,018 answer-side targets (34,652 matched-layer combinations, including chat-template tokens, with/without-template pooling, last-k content tokens, and per-position targets) and scores every combination on the map, direct behavior read-out, and map-mediated read-out, under leave-one-family-out folds, generic UltraChat probes, a disjoint held-out probe pool on both input and target sides, and selection-symmetric null bands.
- **Broader narrative:** The leakage-predictor question (`docs/open_questions.md`, `leak-predictor` anchor) needs one defensible context summary and one answer summary for the base-model context→answer map its theory builds on. This run asks whether any cheaper or sharper read (a single boundary token, a template-block pool) should replace the incumbent whole-answer mean — and finds no separable winner, keeping the incumbent as the default.

## Methodology

**Design:** Nothing is trained. Base `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct`, all 28 decoder blocks, over the fixed 50-context battery (7 families: persona 14 / wildchat 10 / icl 8 / rephrase 6 / format 5 / behavior 5 / default 2). Context summaries: 19 per-layer families (with/without-template mean and max pools, the assistant-header newline, four trailing template tokens, template-block pools, last-k content tokens k = 1..8) plus 10 layer-pooled variants = 542 cells. Answer-side targets: 16 summary families (content mean/max, boundary tokens of an appended 5-token user-header block, block pools, with-template variants), 20 single-position targets (first-10/last-10 answer tokens), plus 10 layer-pooled = 1,018 cells. Matched-layer pairing gives 34,652 map cells. Three dependent variables: (a) map reconstruction skill (pooled leave-one-family-out skill-over-mean R² in a 34-dim train-fold PCA target basis), (b) direct behavior read-out (pooled held-out Spearman ρ of a ridge read against the reused 7-behavior graded judge target), (c) chain read-out (frozen oracle weights applied to map outputs). Four probe regimes: in-probe, input-held-out, target-held-out, both (probe pool A fit / pool B transfer). Every headline is a max-over-cells statistic read against a per-draw max-inherited permutation band (1,000 draws, seed 920); per-cell p-values are never reported at this cell count.

### Behavior read-out clears collapse under the planned family-structure check

The dumbbell plot shows, for each of 28 read-out tests (7 behaviors × context/answer side × two probe regimes), the banded full rank correlation at the best cell (blue) and the same cells' within-family-centered rank correlation (red).

![Full vs family-centered read-out correlations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/09006be091dfb3fb66cf615f0d23d28c169a38b7/figures/issue_920/dv2_full_vs_centered_rho.png)

> **Figure.** *Read-out clears vs the family-structure check.* Blue: banded absolute rank correlation at each best cell (0.52–0.86). Red: after subtracting family means from prediction and target. Median drop ≈55%; a third of reads fall to ≈0. Judge-reliability ceilings 0.68–0.96. n = 50 contexts, 7 families.

27 of 28 tests nominally clear their per-behavior bands (0.49–0.54; reachable, with the correlation ceiling at 1 and reliability ceilings 0.68–0.96). But the behavior target is strongly family-structured (between-family variance fraction 0.31–0.85), predictions cluster by family too, and free permutation assumes exchangeability those clusters violate — the bands are anti-conservative, and the plan itself set a ≈51% family-wise expectation of at least one nominal clear across 28 tests. Family-means-only correlations reach 0.34–1.00; several best cells sit at layer 0–2 template or tail-token reads, a length/format-confound signature. The residual centered signal (refusal ≈0.3–0.5; harmful compliance ≈0.4–0.5, context side) is unbanded and unestablished; the fact-expression read exceeds its 0.72 reliability-consistent maximum on a target with +0.01 external validation. The one non-clear (self-report, context, in-probe: 0.523 vs 0.526) is a failure to reject. The parent's family-held-out read-out collapse stands.

### Chain read-out maxima are selection artifacts, not signal surviving the map

The bar chart shows, per behavior, the oracle-minus-chain correlation gap at the best chain cell (in-probe regime).

![Chain vs oracle gap per behavior](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/09006be091dfb3fb66cf615f0d23d28c169a38b7/figures/issue_920/chain_vs_oracle_gap.png)

At the genuinely good map cells the chain behaves lawfully (chain ≤ oracle, absolute values ≤0.5), so the planned map-induced-loss estimate is not meaningfully identifiable from argmax cells and no chain headline is claimed.
